lecole.name: L'Ecole No 41, 2020 Seven Hills Syrah tech sheet

claims.claim: Budbreak was in mid-April, near the historical average. Summer was moderate and even, with heat spikes in late July and early August.
claims.note: Statewide. Suckling agrees that budbreak and bloom were near normal.

claims.claim: The Washington crop was down sharply, 178,500 tons. Growers pointed to a big 2019 crop, October 2019 freezes and poor fruit set at bloom.
Picking started in the third week of August. A hot early September rushed the early varieties.
Wildfire smoke from Oregon and California reached the region in the second week of September and paused harvest for nearly 10 days. It also slowed sugar buildup.
claims.note: Statewide wording. Suckling confirms the pause.

claims.claim: Walla Walla County air quality passed 400 on the index in mid-September, and some growers sold leftover fruit to wineries elsewhere.
A freeze on October 25 ended the season in many places.
Smoke effects varied. Leonetti declassified fruit from some vineyards. Betz Family did not release a 2020. Other producers tested clean, such as Canvasback for its rosé.
claims.note: The Canvasback and L'Ecole claims are their own statements about their own wines.

claims.claim: Whites and rosés are less exposed to smoke because they spend little or no time on the skins. Oregon winemakers put extra effort into them in 2020.
claims.quote: less exposure to smoke-affected grape skins
claims.note: Oregon source. The reasoning applies to rosé in general, but it is not a Walla Walla finding.

claims.claim: Small berries and long hang time gave dark, concentrated reds for the producers who made wine.

conflicts: Smoke timing: the Wine Commission says second week of September. Union-Bulletin (summary) says mid-September. A Wine Spectator piece from early September says Walla Walla had only a slight haze then, so the heavy smoke came after.
Impact: Quilceda Creek said smoke blew through Red Mountain and Horse Heaven Hills. Walla Walla producers report mixed results.
gaps: No Walla Walla Valley Wine Alliance vintage report found.
No source on Walla Walla rosé picking dates in 2020.
The Union-Bulletin, Canvasback and L'Ecole pages were seen only as search summaries.

sheet.vintage: A small crop, then wildfire smoke in mid-September paused harvest for about 10 days. Rosé spends little time on the skins, which helps in a smoky year.
